name: managed-remote-access-lifecycle-matrix
description: The exhaustive implementer-owned lifecycle ownership matrix for the connector stream registry (THR-097 Unit C fresh lifecycle redesign). Every discovered public membership/ownership mutation is crossed with revocation in BOTH deterministic orderings; each cell states the exact linearization point, the atomic seal+membership transition, callback scope, and the permitted outcome. The contract suite validates this fixture semantically; tests/remote_access encodes the same cells as deterministic public-gateway barrier proofs.
governing_rule: admission and every ownership/membership mutation share one atomic lifecycle boundary: a single lifecycle lock guards the sealed flag AND registry membership; the affected public wrapper(s) are sealed under that boundary before membership/ownership can escape; admissions not fully registered before the revocation seal fail closed and cannot return a usable wrapper; external transport close/open callbacks execute outside locks but remain inside the revocation acknowledgement barrier; revocation may report success only after every pre-seal stream is unusable/closed, all required cleanup outcomes are terminal and acknowledged, and no post-seal admission can return usable. Same-thread re-entrant close_all invoked from an unfinished transport cleanup callback MUST return fail-closed non-success (never success): it may not exclude its own in-flight cleanup and publish success, may not mark the cleanup terminal with an incomplete failed-id set, and may not erase a callback failure that becomes terminal after the re-entrant call; the caller retries close_all from a normal context once its callback's transport close is terminal.

boundary.lifecycle_lock: StreamRegistry._lock guards BOTH the sealed flag (_revoked) and registry membership (_streams)
boundary.atomic_transition: every membership mutation performs its membership transition AND the seal of every affected public wrapper in ONE critical section on the lifecycle lock
boundary.callback_scope: physical transport open/close and duplicate-replacement callbacks execute OUTSIDE the lifecycle lock but INSIDE the revocation acknowledgement barrier
boundary.acknowledgement_barrier: close_all publishes success only after every pre-seal wrapper is sealed, every snapshot transport close is terminal, every in-flight outside-lock transport close that linearized before the seal is terminal, and no post-seal admission can return usable
boundary.seal_first_orderings: when the revocation seal linearizes first, a membership mutation observes the sealed registry: admission fails closed (never returns usable), single/wrapper close is an idempotent no-op (never double-closes the transport), duplicate replacement fails closed without touching sealed membership

linearization_points.admission: the registration insert under the lifecycle lock (sealed-flag check + insert in the SAME critical section)
linearization_points.single_close: the membership pop + wrapper seal under the lifecycle lock (one critical section; no pop-without-seal window)
linearization_points.duplicate_replacement: the old wrapper's pop + seal and the new wrapper's insert under the lifecycle lock (one critical section)
linearization_points.revocation_seal: setting _revoked + sealing every registered wrapper + snapshot + clearing membership under the lifecycle lock, seal before snapshot
linearization_points.retained_wrapper_close: routes through StreamRegistry.close: the same single-close linearization point
linearization_points.fail_closed_admission: the sealed-flag read under the lifecycle lock; the allocated transport is closed outside the lock and never returned

mutations.linearization_point: admission: registration insert under the lifecycle lock
mutations.callbacks: transport allocation/open callbacks outside the lock

orderings.revocation_success_requires: registration included in the close_all snapshot; wrapper irrevocably sealed; physical cleanup outcome terminal and acknowledged before close_all success
orderings.permitted_outcome: registered pre-seal; wrapper revoked with the snapshot; surface reports revocation_stream_closed; no usable wrapper survives

orderings.revocation_success_requires: no post-seal admission returns usable
orderings.permitted_outcome: fail closed: StreamClosed raised; the allocated transport is closed by the registry outside the lock (never leaked, never returned); the gateway returns the normative revocation denial

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: fail-closed admission closes the unregistered allocated handle itself; once a handle is passed to open the registry owns its cleanup and callers (gateway) never double-close

mutations.public_entry: StreamRegistry.open on a sealed registry — admission rejection after seal
mutations.linearization_point: admission: sealed-flag read under the lifecycle lock
mutations.callbacks: the unregistered allocated handle is closed outside the lock; close failure is swallowed (category-only denial already determined)

orderings.revocation_success_requires: no admission after the seal can register
orderings.permitted_outcome: impossible (the registry is already sealed when the admission observes it — this cell exists to pin the fail-closed rule)

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the admission never returns usable and its allocated handle is not left open
orderings.permitted_outcome: StreamClosed raised; handle closed exactly once by the registry; no secret-bearing text in the failure

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: allocated-but-unexposed handle close is attempted to a terminal outcome; the denial is never replaced by a different error

mutations.public_entry: StreamRegistry.open(stream_id, handle) with an existing stream_id — duplicate-id replacement
mutations.membership_effect: replace: remove+seal the old wrapper, register the new wrapper
mutations.seal_scope: old wrapper (same or different inner handle)
mutations.linearization_point: duplicate_replacement: old pop + seal + new insert under the lifecycle lock (one critical section)
mutations.callbacks: the replaced transport close runs OUTSIDE the lock but INSIDE the revocation acknowledgement barrier (close_all waits for it); same-handle re-registration must NOT close the shared inner

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the replaced old wrapper is sealed under the lock; its outside-lock transport close is terminal and acknowledged before close_all success
orderings.permitted_outcome: new wrapper registered pre-seal and revoked with the snapshot (unusable); old wrapper irrevocably sealed; old transport closed exactly once

orderings.revocation_success_requires: no post-seal mutation touches sealed membership
orderings.permitted_outcome: replacement fails closed (StreamClosed); the allocated transport is closed by the registry; the old wrapper remains sealed; no usable stream

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: replaced wrapper's physical cleanup is acknowledged (terminal) before revocation success; a failure is recorded on the replaced wrapper (cleanup_failed) and never blocks the new admission

mutations.linearization_point: single_close: the membership pop + wrapper seal under the lifecycle lock (ONE critical section — there is no pop-without-seal window)
mutations.callbacks: the transport close runs OUTSIDE the lock but INSIDE the revocation acknowledgement barrier

orderings.revocation_success_requires: close_all must NOT publish success while the pre-seal single close's transport close is in flight (acknowledgement barrier); the wrapper is sealed from the moment the mutation linearizes
orderings.permitted_outcome: wrapper irrevocably sealed (receive/send raise StreamClosed, closed reports True) from the linearization point; transport close completes to a terminal outcome before revocation success; no usable wrapper at revocation success

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the post-seal close is an idempotent no-op
orderings.permitted_outcome: idempotent no-op: close returns without effect; the wrapper is already sealed by the revocation snapshot; the transport is closed exactly once (by the snapshot) and never double-closed by the late close

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: the close mutation's caller observes the terminal cleanup outcome (a failing transport close propagates to the caller but never unseals the wrapper); the failed id is PERSISTED on the registry and re-surfaced by a later close_all/revoke (a callback failure that becomes terminal after a re-entrant rejection is never erased); the ack fires when the outside-lock close terminates

mutations.membership_effect: seal the registry + seal every registered wrapper + snapshot + clear membership
mutations.linearization_point: revocation_seal: setting _revoked + sealing wrappers + snapshot under the lifecycle lock, seal before snapshot
mutations.callbacks: every snapshot transport close runs OUTSIDE the lock; same-thread re-entrant close_all from inside a snapshot transport-close callback is rejected with fail-closed non-success (RuntimeError, the public API's existing non-success representation) BEFORE any seal, membership transition, cleanup acknowledgement, or success publication — never an immediate return that publishes success and never a self-inflight exclusion; the callback's own transport close terminates INSIDE the acknowledgement barrier and is acknowledged before the outer run or a later close_all from a normal context reports terminal success or the persisted failure (never erased); concurrent callers wait on the shared terminal result without holding a lock

orderings.revocation_success_requires: self (close_all IS the revocation); snapshot = exactly the pre-seal registrations
orderings.permitted_outcome: every pre-seal wrapper irrevocably sealed; every snapshot transport close terminal (failures persisted as StreamCloseError and re-surfaced by every later close_all); no post-seal admission can register

orderings.revocation_success_requires: self
orderings.permitted_outcome: idempotent: a later close_all observes the persisted terminal result and re-raises persisted failures; never reports success while a cleanup failure relevant to the sealed generation is unreported

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: first caller runs the cleanup exactly once and publishes the shared terminal result; waiters observe the same result; persisted failure ids are re-raised by every subsequent caller

mutations.linearization_point: retained_wrapper_close: the same single-close linearization point (the wrapper is the registry-owned surface; its public close is a registry membership mutation)
mutations.callbacks: the transport close runs OUTSIDE the lock but INSIDE the revocation acknowledgement barrier

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the wrapper close removes membership and seals the wrapper atomically; the transport close is terminal before revocation success
orderings.permitted_outcome: wrapper irrevocably sealed; membership removed; close_all snapshot excludes it; the transport close is acknowledged (terminal) before revocation success and never double-closed by the revocation

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the late wrapper close is an idempotent no-op
orderings.permitted_outcome: idempotent no-op: close returns without effect; the wrapper is already sealed by the revocation snapshot; the transport is closed exactly once (by the snapshot) and never double-closed by the late close

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: same as M4 (the wrapper close is the single-close mutation); the client-held wrapper never escapes the atomic seal

mutations.public_entry: _TrackedStream.close() on an already-sealed wrapper — missing/idempotent close
mutations.linearization_point: the sealed-flag read (single-attribute read; sealed is written only under the lifecycle lock)

orderings.revocation_success_requires: n/a (no mutation)
orderings.permitted_outcome: no-op; never raises; never re-closes the transport

orderings.revocation_success_requires: n/a
orderings.permitted_outcome: no-op; the revocation transaction owns cleanup after sealing

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: n/a — the wrapper is already terminal

mutations.public_entry: _TrackedStream.receive() / send() / closed / status / headers — derived wrapper surface
mutations.linearization_point: the wrapper-surface read itself: a sealed wrapper rejects receive/send and reports closed=True; the seal is atomic under the lifecycle lock so a read linearizes either before (pre-seal state) or after (post-seal fail-closed state) the seal

orderings.revocation_success_requires: post-seal reads fail closed
orderings.permitted_outcome: receive/send raise StreamClosed; closed reports True; cleanup_failed reports evidence without claiming physical closure

orderings.revocation_success_requires: same
orderings.permitted_outcome: same fail-closed surface; no retained reference is ever readable/writable after the seal

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: n/a — the wrapper surface is owned by the registry; the seal write is under the lifecycle lock and surface reads are single-attribute reads

mutations.linearization_point: the membership read under the lifecycle lock

orderings.revocation_success_requires: post-seal reads report the sealed truth
orderings.permitted_outcome: is_open False for every removed/sealed stream; raise_if_open raises StreamClosed for absent membership

orderings.revocation_success_requires: same
orderings.permitted_outcome: is_open False for every stream after close_all; raise_if_open raises StreamClosed

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: n/a — reads only, synchronized on the lifecycle lock

mutations.public_entry: same-thread re-entrant close_all from inside a transport-close callback (during close_all's own cleanup OR inside a single-close's outside-lock transport close)
mutations.membership_effect: none (rejected — fail-closed non-success; no seal, no membership change, no publish)
mutations.linearization_point: the same-thread re-entrancy rejection at close_all entry (self-inflight / in-cleanup guard): the re-entrant call returns the existing non-success representation BEFORE any seal, membership transition, or acknowledgement publish
mutations.callbacks: the callback is running OUTSIDE the lifecycle lock inside an unfinished transport cleanup callback (its own close is not yet terminal)

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the re-entrant call never deadlocks, never publishes success, never marks _cleanup_done with an incomplete failed-id set, and never excludes its own in-flight cleanup; a callback failure that becomes terminal AFTER the rejection is persisted and re-surfaced by a later close_all
orderings.permitted_outcome: the re-entrant close_all is rejected with fail-closed non-success (the public API's existing non-success representation — RuntimeError, mirroring the coordinator's re-entrant-revoke rejection) BEFORE any seal, membership transition, or acknowledgement publish; the registry is left unsealed and unpublished (no false success acknowledgement, no incomplete failed-id set); the callback completes its own transport close to a terminal outcome; a later close_all from a normal context reports the terminal success or the PERSISTED failure (never erased)

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the re-entrant call never deadlocks and never corrupts the terminal result; the outer cleanup run owns and publishes the complete terminal result
orderings.permitted_outcome: the re-entrant close_all is rejected with fail-closed non-success (the public API's existing non-success representation — RuntimeError, mirroring the coordinator's re-entrant-revoke rejection); the outer run continues and publishes the terminal result; a callback that does not handle the rejection makes its own close fail closed (recorded in the terminal failed-id set)

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: the re-entrant call acknowledges and publishes NOTHING; the outer run (or a later normal-context close_all) owns the acknowledgement; barrier-tracked close failures are folded into the persisted terminal failed-id set before publish — never published with an incomplete set

mutations.public_entry: same-thread re-entrant RevocationCoordinator.revoke from inside a transport-close callback
mutations.linearization_point: the thread-local re-entrancy guard at revoke entry
mutations.callbacks: the callback runs outside the transaction lock

orderings.revocation_success_requires: re-entry fails closed without deadlock
orderings.permitted_outcome: RuntimeError (re-entrant revocation transaction rejected)

orderings.revocation_success_requires: same
orderings.permitted_outcome: RuntimeError

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: the outer revoke owns the transaction; the re-entrant call is rejected

mutations.public_entry: concurrent close_all callers — waiters observing the shared terminal result
mutations.membership_effect: one caller runs the cleanup; the rest wait
mutations.linearization_point: the runner's seal + snapshot under the lifecycle lock; the waiters' observation of the persisted terminal result
mutations.callbacks: the runner's transport closes run outside the lock; waiters hold no lock while waiting

orderings.revocation_success_requires: every waiter observes the same terminal result; a same-thread transport-close callback re-entering close_all while another caller's cleanup is in progress is REJECTED with fail-closed non-success (it must never wait on the shared completion event — waiting would self-deadlock the acknowledgement barrier); the runner still publishes the complete terminal result
orderings.permitted_outcome: all waiters see the persisted failed ids / success; a racing higher-epoch revoke can never treat an in-flight closure as a successful no-op

orderings.revocation_success_requires: same; a same-thread transport-close callback re-entering close_all while another caller's cleanup is in progress is REJECTED with fail-closed non-success (it must never wait on the shared completion event — waiting would self-deadlock the acknowledgement barrier); the runner still publishes the complete terminal result
orderings.permitted_outcome: same — later callers re-raise persisted failures

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: the complete cleanup terminal result is shared/persisted; no caller returns success while a cleanup failure relevant to the sealed generation is unreported; a callback re-entering close_all on the same thread while another caller's cleanup is in progress returns fail-closed non-success rather than waiting on the shared event; pre-seal explicit-close failures persisted on the registry are folded into the published failed-id set

mutations.linearization_point: revocation_seal (inside close_all) precedes trust-state application; the epoch advance validates rollback before any side effect
mutations.callbacks: transport closes run outside locks; a callback re-entering revoke fails closed (RuntimeError); a callback re-entering the registry's close_all directly is likewise rejected (fail-closed non-success) — the coordinator guard fires first within revoke

orderings.revocation_success_requires: seal first, snapshot second, cleanup acknowledged, THEN trust-state application; the transaction re-surfaces ANY persisted registry failure (including a pre-seal explicit-close failure recorded on the registry) as RevocationIncomplete with the applied epoch — never erased
orderings.permitted_outcome: revoke returns the applied epoch, or RevocationIncomplete with applied epoch + failed stream ids when a handle close failed (state still revoked)

orderings.revocation_success_requires: later revoke re-validates the epoch advance (rollback rejected) and re-surfaces persisted failures; the transaction re-surfaces ANY persisted registry failure (including a pre-seal explicit-close failure recorded on the registry) as RevocationIncomplete with the applied epoch — never erased
orderings.permitted_outcome: higher-epoch revoke re-raises the persisted failed ids (never false success); rollback rejected before any side effect

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: the transaction serializes concurrent revocations and persists the complete cleanup terminal result; RevocationIncomplete carries the applied epoch and failed stream ids; pre-seal explicit-close failures persisted on the registry are folded into the transaction's failed-id report (never erased)

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: guarded idempotent inner close; registry owns the wrapper lifecycle regardless of transport self-close

mutations.public_entry: transport-close callback invoking a registry mutation (open / close / close_all) during revocation cleanup
mutations.membership_effect: open fails closed; close is a no-op; close_all is rejected (fail-closed non-success via the same-thread guard)
mutations.linearization_point: the registry sealed-flag/membership read under the lifecycle lock (callbacks run outside the lock)
mutations.callbacks: the callback IS the transport close callback; it executes OUTSIDE the lifecycle lock and never deadlocks

orderings.revocation_success_requires: the callback's mutation observes the sealed registry
orderings.permitted_outcome: open fails closed (allocated handle closed by the registry); close is an idempotent no-op; close_all raises the fail-closed non-success rejection (RuntimeError); revoke raises RuntimeError

orderings.revocation_success_requires: same
orderings.permitted_outcome: open fails closed (allocated handle closed by the registry); close is an idempotent no-op; close_all raises the fail-closed non-success rejection (RuntimeError); revoke raises RuntimeError

mutations.cleanup_acknowledgement: the outer revocation owns the terminal result; the re-entrant close_all never publishes or acknowledges; callback mutations never corrupt or bypass it

notes: The matrix is exhaustive over every ownership/membership path discovered by the producer-complete rg audit of runtime/remote_access (streams.py StreamRegistry.open/close/close_all/is_open/raise_if_open, _TrackedStream.close; revocation.py RevocationCoordinator.revoke; gateway.py ConnectorGateway._forward admission/EOF/error paths and _close_partial; forwarding.py transport self-close and guarded idempotent close).

Cells M1-M19 are encoded as deterministic PUBLIC-GATEWAY barrier proofs in tests/remote_access (not registry-only lookalikes) with entered/release barrier events, no timing sleeps, and assertions on wrapper receive/send/closed state, inner transport state/close counts, registry membership, revocation return/error, and no false-success acknowledgement.

Checked-in mutation proofs remove/bypass the unified boundary (pop without seal, seal outside the boundary, close_all success before acknowledgement, wrapper close not routed through the registry) — each mutation must go red.

Unit-A threat cases REV-004/REV-005/REV-006/REV-007/REV-008 encode the admission-vs-seal and single-close-vs-seal permitted outcomes; REV-005 and REV-006 are the machine-readable close-vs-revoke cells.

THR-097 seq140 founder ruling: same-thread re-entrant close_all from an unfinished transport cleanup callback fails closed with non-success (never success, never an incomplete failed-id publish, never a self-inflight exclusion), and a callback failure that becomes terminal after the re-entrant rejection is persisted and re-surfaced by a later close_all/revoke (REV-007/REV-008).
